# The AI tools

Every tool Faro’s MCP server offers an AI assistant: what it does, the arguments it takes (its JSON schema), what it gives back, the words it refuses with, and the actions that do the same in the app. An assistant can do whatever its person can, and no more: a token acts as one person in one workspace, with that person’s rights ([R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md), rule 5), so who may run a tool is who may run [the actions](actions.md) it does. Read from the code by `src/spec/calls.ts`: the schemas are `TOOLS` in `src/mcp/tools.ts` (with each module’s tools), what a tool gives back is the type of the `data` its run returns, and the refusals are every sentence its run can throw or return as an error.

## What every tool shares

- **The protocol** is MCP over HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0): `tools/list` gives every tool below with its schema, `tools/call` runs one. The token is a bearer token, made by an admin for one person and kept only as its hash.
- **The arguments** are checked against the schema; no argument outside it is accepted (`additionalProperties: false`). A goal is named by its id or its key (`G-12`), a person by name or id.
- **What it gives back:** a text for the assistant to read, in plain words with each status’s code beside its word (“Off track (off)”), and, for most tools, `data` beside it (MCP structured content), typed below. A tool that sends pictures sends them after the text.
- **A change** goes through the same rules as the app’s: the change engine for check-ins, goals, plans, bulk changes and spreadsheets, so it raises [the same issues](import-issues.md) and asks the same questions. `dry_run: true` shows what would change and saves nothing; `confirm: true` goes ahead past a question once the person has said so; `answers` answers the engine’s questions. Every change is logged as the token’s person, marked via MCP, and can be undone as the app’s can.
- **A refusal** comes back as a tool error (`isError`) with words to show; nothing is saved. A refusal by a rule ends with who the token acts as: “This token acts as …, who is an admin.” or “… who isn’t an admin.” Every tool can also say: “There’s no tool called ….”; “… is switched off in …, so … can’t be used there. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.”. Its own refusals are listed under each tool, and the refusals of the actions it does the same as are on [the actions](actions.md).
- **The hints** (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`) are MCP annotations: shown below as reads, changes, or changes and removes something.

## get_overview

**Overview of the goals.** A short brief of every goal in the current cycle: what needs attention and why, every goal by what it feeds, open questions and actions, and each goal’s weekly numbers. Start here.

**Kind:** reads. Hints: readOnlyHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

No arguments.

<details><summary>The input schema, as JSON</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

**Gives back:** the text only.

**Refuses with:** nothing of its own beyond the shared refusals above.

**Does the same as:** no action: it reads, or does something only an assistant needs.

## find_goals

**Find goals.** List goals in the current cycle with their key (G-12), ID, status (the words people see, with the code: “Off track (off)”), latest number, this week’s plan, target and gap. Filter by whose goals they are (scope: mine, team, watching or all, as the Goals screen’s tabs), words in the name or a key, owner, status or level, or only the goals on the Needs attention list (flagged for something new that nobody has picked up yet, then those being handled below them, marked: the same rule as Home, Watching and reviews); or pass the query of a shared Goals link, or the name of a saved view, for every filter and sort the Goals screen has. A goal’s key and its ID both work wherever a tool asks for a goal. Answers as JSON, the same keys every time: week, weeks, total (how many match), offset, goals (at most limit of them, 50 unless asked), more (how to ask for the next page, or null) and why (why nothing matches, or null).

**Kind:** reads. Hints: readOnlyHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | Words on the goal’s row (its name, key, owner, team, level, status, reason or definition), each the start of a word; or its key (G-12). |
| `owner` | string | no | Part of the owner’s name. |
| `status` | string | no | Only goals with this status: the words or the code, any of Off track (off), At risk (risk), No recent update (stale), No check-in yet (none), On track (on), Done (done), Not started (planned). |
| `needs_attention` | boolean | no | Only the goals on the Needs attention list: those that need attention first, then those being handled (beingHandled says how), as the Goals screen lists them. A goal needs attention when it is off track, missed its own date, no recent update, decision or help needed, no path to green, at risk, getting worse or greener than calculated, unless someone is already handling it. The same rule picks the goals on Home, in Watching, on the map, in the Goals filter, in reviews and for the AI assistant. Wherever they are listed, the goals being handled are listed below them, so nothing is hidden; a count of goals that need attention leaves those out. |
| `level` | one of `north-star`, `svp`, `team` | no | Only goals at this level. |
| `mine` | boolean | no | Only goals you own (the same as scope "mine"). |
| `scope` | one of `mine`, `team`, `watching`, `all` | no | Whose goals, as the Goals screen’s tabs have them: mine (goals you own), team (your team’s and the teams you lead), watching (goals you watch, directly or through a tree or a level) or all (the default). A scope you don’t have (team when you’re in no team and lead none, mine when you own none) finds no goals and says why. |
| `query` | string | no | A Goals link’s query string, e.g. "scope=mine&status=off,risk&attention=1&needs=decision&due=quarter&sort=gap". Keys: scope (as the scope argument, which wins if both are given), q, status (Off track (off), At risk (risk), No recent update (stale), No check-in yet (none), On track (on), Done (done), Not started (planned)), level (north-star, svp, team), team and owner (IDs), kind (metric, range, milestone), attention (1: the Needs attention list, those being handled below the rest), needs (because: Off track (off), Missed its own date (missed-path), No recent update (stale), Decision or help needed (decision), No path to green (no-path), At risk (risk), Getting worse (trend), Greener than calculated (greener), Date slipped (slipped)), due (quarter or a week), quiet (no update for this many weeks), qtr (Met (met), Not met (missed)), result (Met (completed), Met late (late), Not met (missed), Not finished yet (open)), feeds (a goal ID: its tree), helps (1), sort (worst, title, owner, team, level, gap, last, due; add .desc to reverse). |
| `view` | string | no | The name of a saved view: one of yours, or one pinned for everyone. |
| `state` | one of `active`, `proposed` | no | active (the default) or proposed: proposed goals have no status and are listed only when asked for. |
| `limit` | integer | no | How many goals to list, from offset: 50 unless asked, at most 200. |
| `offset` | integer | no | How many matching goals to skip, for the next page (as “more” says). |

**Refuses with:**

## get_goal

**One goal in full.** Everything about one goal: its scorecard as the goal’s page shows it (vs plan, vs last week, to target, and whether it will hit the target), its plan by week, every check-in with the owner’s reasons, notes, questions and actions from reviews, and its comments (with their IDs, for edit_comment and delete_comment).

**Kind:** reads. Hints: readOnlyHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goal_id` | string | yes | The goal’s ID or its key (e.g. G-12), from find_goals. |

<details><summary>The input schema, as JSON</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "goal_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "goal_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The goal’s ID or its key (e.g. G-12), from find_goals."
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

**Gives back:** the text, and `data`, one of:

```ts
{
    cycle: {

        quarters?: {
            label: string;

            from: number;
            to: number;
        }[] | undefined;
```

**Refuses with:**

**Does the same as:** no action: it reads, or does something only an assistant needs.

## post_check_in

**Post a check-in.** Post the number (or stages) for one goal for a week: this week by default, or an earlier week to fill in history. The same rules as the app apply: behind or ahead of plan needs a cause and a why; at risk or off track needs a path to green. Only the goal’s owner can post: not an admin, and not anyone else (an admin brings others’ check-ins in only by loading a workbook, or corrects a past one in Data’s tables). Posting again for the same week corrects that week’s check-in (the log keeps both).

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goal_id` | string | yes | The goal’s ID or its key, e.g. G-12. |
| `week` | integer | no | The week, counted from the cycle start. Defaults to this week. Earlier weeks are marked as loaded later. |
| `value` | number | no | Number goals: the value for the week. |
| `stages` | string | no | Milestone goals: e.g. "Pilot: done week 6; Rollout: expected week 9". |
| `call` | string | no | The owner’s status call, in the words or the code: On track (on), At risk (risk), Off track (off), Done (done). Leave out to let the rules decide. |
| `cause` | one of `Plan too aggressive`, `Delivery slower`, `Blocked by a dependency`, `External factor`, `Data problem`, `Plan too cautious`, `Change landed early`, `One-off, won’t last` | no | Why it’s behind or ahead. |
| `why` | string | no | In a sentence (10 characters or more). |
| `why_greener` | string | no | If the call is greener than calculated: why. |
| `path_to_green` | string | no | How it gets back on plan. |
| `recovery` | one of `Plan`, `Still investigating`, `Needs a decision or help`, `Target should change` | no | Where the owner is with recovery. |
| `back_on_plan_by_week` | integer | no | With a plan: the week it is back on plan by. |
| `needs` | string | no | A decision or help needed, and from whom. |
| `next_step` | string | no | The next step. |
| `reason` | string | no | If the week already has a check-in, this corrects it: why, in a sentence (10 to 500 characters), kept as “Why corrected”. |
| `answers` | object | no | Answers to the questions (Check) a dry run asked, by the group id it gave: {"<id>": "<choice>"} or {"<id>": {"choice": "choose", "value": "Platform"}}. One answer covers every row in its group. Ask the person; never answer for them. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Check the change without saving it. Use it to see what would change, or what is missing. |

## update_goal

**Change a goal.** Change a goal’s details or plan. Only the fields you give change. A plan change (start, target, shape, due week, limit, stages) after check-ins have started needs a reason, which is logged with the old and new plan. One that flips which way is better, or puts a number far outside the old plan, is checked with the person first (confirm: true).

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goal_id` | string | yes | The goal’s ID or its key, e.g. G-12. |
| `title` | string | no | The goal’s name. |
| `owner` | string | no | The owner’s full name, as in the workspace (when only one person has it; owner_email is exact). |
| `owner_email` | string | no | The owner’s email: exact, even where two people share a name. |
| `team` | string | no | The team’s name. |
| `level` | one of `north star`, `svp`, `team` | no | How important it is for reporting. |
| `unit` | string | no | Number goals: the unit, e.g. "%", "days", "USD". |
| `decimals` | integer | no | Number goals: decimal places, 0 to 3. |
| `start` | number | no | Move-a-number goals: where it starts. |
| `target` | number | no | Move-a-number goals: the target. |
| `plan_shape` | one of `straight`, `back-loaded`, `stepped` | no | Move-a-number goals: how the plan moves from start to target. |
| `from` | string | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the baseline (start) was true and the plan starts, as a year and a week, e.g. "2026-W46". Left out: this week for a new goal. |
| `to` | string | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the target is due, as a year and a week, e.g. "2027-W13": up to the last week of next year. Left out: the end of this goal year. |
| `due_week` | integer | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the target is due, counted from the cycle start (the older form of to; weeks beyond the cycle run into the next goal year). |
| `limit` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals: the limit; for a range between two numbers, the upper one. |
| `lower` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals between two numbers ("keep it between 99.5 and 99.95"): the lower one, below limit. Giving it makes must_stay "between". |
| `must_stay` | one of `at most`, `at least`, `between` | no | Keep-in-range goals: which side of the limit is good, or between lower and limit. |
| `margin` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals: how close to the limit counts as at risk. |
| `stages` | list of string | no | Milestone goals: each stage as "Name@week", e.g. "Pilot@6". |
| `feeds_into_id` | string | no | The ID or key (G-12) of the goal this one feeds. Empty string to unlink. |
| `why_it_helps` | string | no | Why we expect it to help the goal it feeds. |
| `source` | string | no | Where the number comes from. |
| `definition` | string | no | Exactly what is counted. |
| `state` | one of `active`, `proposed` | no | active (the default for a new goal) or proposed: a proposed goal is visible to everyone, has no status and nothing due, and needs no plan yet; its owner or an admin makes it active (make_goal_active). A goal with check-ins can’t go back to proposed. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why the plan is changing. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | True once the person has said yes to every question a goal was asked (Check: a number that looks unlikely, no unit, a link to a lower level, a plan change that flips which way is better or is far outside the old plan). |
| `answers` | object | no | Answers to the questions (Check) a dry run asked, by the group id it gave: {"<id>": "<choice>"} or {"<id>": {"choice": "choose", "value": "Platform"}}. One answer covers every row in its group. Ask the person; never answer for them. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Check the change without saving it. Use it to see what would change, or what is missing. |

## make_goal_active

**Make a proposed goal active.** Its owner or an admin: make a proposed goal active. A number goal’s plan runs from this week, or from the week given. From then it is judged against its plan and check-ins are due. Use dry_run first to read back the dates and when the first check-in is due, and say it to the person.

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goal_id` | string | yes | The goal’s ID or its key, e.g. G-12. |
| `from` | string | no | Number goals: the week its plan runs from, as a year and a week (2026-W48) or the week’s number. Left out: this week. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | True once the person has said the goal has been running since an earlier From (the question comes back otherwise). |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Check the change without saving it. Use it to see what would change, or what is missing. |

## create_goal

**Add a goal.** Add a goal to the current cycle. Type "metric" moves a number from start to target; "range" keeps a number inside a limit; "milestone" hits dated stages. Anyone may add a goal for anyone, at any level; only its owner or an admin can change it afterwards. Give a unit for a number. What is possible but unlikely (no unit, over 100%, a target a hundred times the start, a link to a lower level) is a question: ask the person, then call again with "confirm": true (a name another goal in its team has is asked through "answers").

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | one of `metric`, `range`, `milestone` | yes | What kind of goal. |
| `title` | string | yes | The goal’s name. |
| `owner` | string | no | The owner’s full name, as in the workspace (when only one person has it; owner_email is exact). |
| `owner_email` | string | no | The owner’s email: exact, even where two people share a name. |
| `team` | string | no | The team’s name. |
| `level` | one of `north star`, `svp`, `team` | no | How important it is for reporting. |
| `unit` | string | no | Number goals: the unit, e.g. "%", "days", "USD". |
| `decimals` | integer | no | Number goals: decimal places, 0 to 3. |
| `start` | number | no | Move-a-number goals: where it starts. |
| `target` | number | no | Move-a-number goals: the target. |
| `plan_shape` | one of `straight`, `back-loaded`, `stepped` | no | Move-a-number goals: how the plan moves from start to target. |
| `from` | string | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the baseline (start) was true and the plan starts, as a year and a week, e.g. "2026-W46". Left out: this week for a new goal. |
| `to` | string | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the target is due, as a year and a week, e.g. "2027-W13": up to the last week of next year. Left out: the end of this goal year. |
| `due_week` | integer | no | Move-a-number goals: the week the target is due, counted from the cycle start (the older form of to; weeks beyond the cycle run into the next goal year). |
| `limit` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals: the limit; for a range between two numbers, the upper one. |
| `lower` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals between two numbers ("keep it between 99.5 and 99.95"): the lower one, below limit. Giving it makes must_stay "between". |
| `must_stay` | one of `at most`, `at least`, `between` | no | Keep-in-range goals: which side of the limit is good, or between lower and limit. |
| `margin` | number | no | Keep-in-range goals: how close to the limit counts as at risk. |
| `stages` | list of string | no | Milestone goals: each stage as "Name@week", e.g. "Pilot@6". |
| `feeds_into_id` | string | no | The ID or key (G-12) of the goal this one feeds. Empty string to unlink. |
| `why_it_helps` | string | no | Why we expect it to help the goal it feeds. |
| `source` | string | no | Where the number comes from. |
| `definition` | string | no | Exactly what is counted. |
| `state` | one of `active`, `proposed` | no | active (the default for a new goal) or proposed: a proposed goal is visible to everyone, has no status and nothing due, and needs no plan yet; its owner or an admin makes it active (make_goal_active). A goal with check-ins can’t go back to proposed. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | True once the person has said yes to every question a goal was asked (Check: a number that looks unlikely, no unit, a link to a lower level, a plan change that flips which way is better or is far outside the old plan). |
| `answers` | object | no | Answers to the questions (Check) a dry run asked, by the group id it gave: {"<id>": "<choice>"} or {"<id>": {"choice": "choose", "value": "Platform"}}. One answer covers every row in its group. Ask the person; never answer for them. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Check the change without saving it. Use it to see what would change, or what is missing. |

## bulk_change

**Change many goals at once.** Add or change many people, goals, plan numbers and check-ins in one go, using the same columns as the spreadsheet export and export_table (e.g. goals: [{"Key": "G-12", "Target": 90}], check_ins: [{"Goal key": "G-12", "Week": 3, "Value": 41}], plan: [{"Key": "G-12", "Week 5": 45}], people: [{"Email": "ana@example.com", "Job title": "Staff engineer"}]). A goal is found by its Key, then its ID (a key works wherever an ID does: Goal key, Feeds into key, Feeds into ID); a goal this same call adds, by its row's Ref: give each new goal a "Ref" of your own and name it in "Feeds into ref" or a check-in's "Goal ref", so one dry run builds a whole tree with its first numbers (goals: [{"Ref": "top", "Goal": "…"}, {"Ref": "a", "Goal": "…", "Feeds into ref": "top"}], check_ins: [{"Goal ref": "a", "Week": 46, "Value": 12}]); a person by Email, then a name only one person has (Owner email is exact). Columns a row leaves out stay as they are; worked-out columns (Status, Calculated…) are ignored. An Action column does what the app does: Stop (with a Reason) or Delete on a goal, Left (with Takes over, by email) on a person. Checks every row and returns what would change, and every problem by kind: must_fix (fix the rows) and check (questions: ask the person, then call again with "answers" by group id; one answer covers every row in its group); nothing is saved unless "apply" is true and every row is valid, and it can be undone (undo_import).

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goals` | list of object | no | Rows for the Goals sheet. Key (or ID) to change a goal; neither to add one. |
| `plan` | list of object | no | Rows for the Plan sheet: Key (or ID), Start and "Week N" columns. |
| `check_ins` | list of object | no | Rows for the Check-ins sheet: Goal key (or Goal ID), Week, Value or Stages, Call, Cause, Why, Why greener, Path to green, Recovery, Back on plan by week, Needs, Next step; ID to correct one check-in. |
| `people` | list of object | no | Rows for the People sheet (admins): Email (or ID) to change someone; a new Email, Name and Team to add someone; Action and Takes over to mark someone as left. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why plans are changing, for any plan change that needs one. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | True once the person has said yes to every question a goal was asked (Check: a number that looks unlikely, no unit, a link to a lower level, a plan change that flips which way is better or is far outside the old plan). |
| `answers` | object | no | Answers to the questions (Check) a dry run asked, by the group id it gave: {"<id>": "<choice>"} or {"<id>": {"choice": "choose", "value": "Platform"}}. One answer covers every row in its group. Ask the person; never answer for them. |
| `apply` | boolean | no | Save the changes. Leave out first to check them. |

## review_call

**Say something in a review.** In a review, about one goal: mark it reviewed (acknowledge), add a note, ask the owner a question, agree an action (who and by when), or accept the risk on a goal behind (accept, with the reason as text). A goal off track or at risk leaves a review with a decision: an action with who and due_week, or accept. Logged in this session of the review. A question or an action is an ask: open until it’s answered (answer_request) or done (mark_action_done), or withdrawn.

## save_review

**Set up or change a review.** Set up a review (anyone can), or change one (someone in it, whoever set it up, or an admin): its name, how often, the weekday, the goals it walks (goals, goals with everything feeding them, or whole levels) and who’s in it. Without review_id it sets up a new one.

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `review_id` | string | no | The review to change. Leave out to set up a new one. |
| `name` | string | no | Its name, e.g. "Platform weekly review". |
| `every_weeks` | integer | no | Held every 1, 2 or 4 weeks. |
| `weekday` | one of `Monday`, `Tuesday`, `Wednesday`, `Thursday`, `Friday` | no | The weekday. |

## start_next_cycle

**Start the next cycle.** Admins, from the day the wrap-up opens: set up the next cycle with the goals that carry on. Nobody moves into it until the current cycle’s last day, and it can be undone (undo_start_cycle) until someone uses it. Without confirm (a dry run, the default) it changes nothing and returns what would carry on, finish and stop, in counts that add up to every goal. Ask the person first, then call again with confirm: true.

**Kind:** changes; removes something. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | True (the default): only say what starting would do. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | True, once the person has said to start it. |

<details><summary>The input schema, as JSON</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True (the default): only say what starting would do."
    },
    "confirm": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True, once the person has said to start it."
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

**Gives back:** the text, and `data`, one of:

```ts
{
    carried?: number | undefined;
    total?: number | undefined;
    next: string;
    canStart: boolean;
    whyNot: string | null;
    counts: {
        n: number;
        says: string;
        sub: string;
    }[];
}
```

```ts
{
    name: string;
}
```

**Refuses with:** nothing of its own beyond the shared refusals above.

**Does the same as:** [startNextCycle](actions.md#startnextcycle), so it refuses with their words too.

## save_table_view

**Save a data table’s layout.** Save a layout of one of Data’s tables (goals, checkIns, plan, requests, people) as a named saved layout, as the Data screen does: the columns to show, in order (the table’s name column always comes first), their widths in pixels, and its search, filters and sort.     "widths": {
```json
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "number"
      },
      "description": "Column widths in pixels by column name, e.g. {\"Owner\": 200}. Kept between each column’s least width (56 to 120) and 640."
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Search, filters and sort as the Data link carries them, e.g. \"q=pipeline&f=Owner~is~Maya Chen&s=Week~desc\". Filter conditions: is, isNot, contains, notContains, eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, empty, notEmpty; several values for is or isNot separated by |."
```

## set_feature

**Switch a feature on or off.** Admins: switch one of Faro's optional features (its modules) on or off in this workspace. Off, it leaves every screen: no page, menu or tool of its own, here or for assistants; anything that needs it goes off with it. Nothing it saved is deleted, and switching it back on brings it all back. The change is logged. The features: metrics (Metric library: Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company.); spreadsheets (Spreadsheets: Download the goals as an Excel workbook or CSV files, and load changes back from a spreadsheet, with every change shown before it’s saved.).

## stop_goal

**Stop a goal.** The goal’s owner or an admin: stop a goal that has check-ins, mid-cycle, with a reason. ## undo_import

**Undo an import or bulk edit.** Whoever made it, or an admin: put every row an import, bulk edit or bulk_change wrote back as it was. Goals and check-ins it added are deleted; ones it changed get their earlier version back. Rows changed since stay as they are and are listed with why. With dry_run, nothing is saved: it says how many rows would go back and which would stay, so you can tell the person first. Import IDs are in get_activity (kind=imports).

**Kind:** changes; removes something. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint false.

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |

```json
  ],

      "type": "string",
      "description": "The import’s ID (imp_…), from get_activity."

    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Say what Undo would do without saving anything."

}
```

## review_inbox

**Review the inbox.** Everything new in the inbox in one step, ready to triage: new markups grouped by the screen part they are about (newest first, with a count), each with its line, notes, who sent it and from where, and new feedback grouped by page. The newest markup of each group comes with its picture as an image. Then use update_markup and update_feedback.

**Kind:** reads. Hints: readOnlyHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

## save_metric

**Add or change a metric.** Add a metric to the library (anyone; you own it unless you name an owner), or change one by giving its id (its owner or an admin). A new metric needs a name, a unit and a direction; everything else is optional. Fields left out keep their value. Saving it unchanged saves nothing. Changing the unit or direction of a metric goals use is refused with a question: ask the person, then call again with confirm: true. A likely mistake is questioned before anything is saved (a name one letter or a word from another metric’s, or one a metric used to have; a unit spelt differently from one in use; a percentage whose meaning doesn’t say out of what): the call returns `checks`, each with its question and answers, and saves nothing. Ask the person, then call again with `answers`. The result says what the metric still needs to say (“Fully defined”, or “Still to say: …”); it is never a score.

From the [metrics](../modules/metrics/README.md) module: switched off with it.

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | no | The metric to change, by ID or name. Leave out to add one. |
| `name` | string | no | Its name, e.g. “Build time (p90)”. Required for a new metric; no two metrics share one. |
| `meaning` | string | no | What it means and how it’s calculated: what is counted, over what period, what is left out. |
| `unit` | string | no | Its unit: %, min, hours, USD, deploys… Required for a new metric. A goal it measures must use the same unit. |
| `decimals` | integer | no | Places after the decimal point it’s shown with (0 to 4; 0 when left out). |
| `direction` | one of `higher`, `lower` | no | Which way is better. Required for a new metric. |
| `source` | string | no | Where the number comes from: a dashboard, a tool, a query. |
| `source_owner` | string | no | Who owns that source: a team or a person, as text. |
| `refresh` | one of `live`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `` | no | How often the source refreshes. Empty for not said. |
| `owner` | string | no | Who answers for the definition, by ID, email or name. Whoever adds it, when left out. |
| `caveats` | string | no | What to watch out for when reading it. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | Yes to changing the unit or direction of a metric goals use, once the person has said so. |
| `answers` | object | no | The person’s answers to the checks a previous call returned. |
| `answers.name` | string | no | “keep:<id>” (mine is different from that metric), or “use:<id>” to use that metric instead (nothing is saved), with the id the question gave. |
| `answers.unit` | one of `keep`, `use` | no | “keep” the unit as typed, or “use” the one in use. |
| `answers.meaning` | one of `as-written` | no | “as-written”: the meaning is right as written. |

```json
      "description": "Which way is better. Required for a new metric.",
      "enum": [
        "higher",
        "lower"
      ]
    },

      "type": "string",
      "description": "Where the number comes from: a dashboard, a tool, a query."
    },
```

## link_goal_metric

**Say which metric measures a goal.** Measure a goal by a metric, for a slice: a team’s number (team) or the whole company’s (team left out), and optionally one part of it (part). A first call that raises a question saves nothing and returns `checks`; call again with `answers`. Or give unlink true to stop measuring it by one. The goal’s owner or an admin. The goal must have a number (not dated stages) in the metric’s unit; its own target is the target in that metric. A goal aiming the other way from the metric’s better direction is allowed, with a warning. Linking again the same way changes nothing.

From the [metrics](../modules/metrics/README.md) module: switched off with it.

**Kind:** changes. Hints: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false.

| `goal` | string | yes | The goal’s ID or key (G-12). |
| `metric` | string | no | The metric’s ID or name. Required unless unlinking. |
| `team` | string | no | The slice: a team by ID or name. Leave out for the whole company. |
| `part` | string | no | Which part of that number, up to 60 characters (“tier-1 services”, a region). Leave out or empty for all of it. Reuse a part other goals on the metric use: get_metric lists them. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why the goal is measured differently now. Required when a goal with check-ins changes its metric, team or part; it shows in the goal’s History. |
| `answers` | object | no | Answers to the checks a first call returned: part ("keep" or "use:<part>"), others ("carry-on": another goal already measures the same number). |
| `answers.part` | string | no |  |
| `answers.others` | string | no |  |
| `unlink` | boolean | no | Stop measuring the goal by its metric. |

| `format` | one of `json`, `brief`, `goals_csv`, `plan_csv`, `check_ins_csv`, `people_csv`, `results_csv`, `asks_csv`, `notes_csv`, `metrics_csv` | yes | Which export. |

The records it names: [DisplayStatus](data-model.md#displaystatus), [StageUpdate](data-model.md#stageupdate), [Status](data-model.md#status), [Cause](data-model.md#cause), [RecoveryState](data-model.md#recoverystate), [PlanShape](data-model.md#planshape), [AskStatus](data-model.md#askstatus).

**Refuses with:**

- “format should be json, brief or one of ….”

**Does the same as:** no action: it reads, or does something only an assistant needs.

## export_table

**Export a data table as shown.** One of Data’s tables (goals, checkIns, plan, requests, people) exactly as a layout shows it: its columns in order and the rows that pass its search and filters, sorted, then any column that says which record a row is (a goal’s Key and ID, a person’s Email…) the layout leaves out, so the rows load back with bulk_change. Give a saved layout by name, or the table with columns and a query. CSV by default, or rows as JSON.

From the [spreadsheets](../modules/spreadsheets/README.md) module: switched off with it.

**Kind:** reads. Hints: readOnlyHint true, openWorldHint false.

**Input:**

| Argument | Type | Needed | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | no | The name of a saved layout: one of yours, or one pinned for everyone. |
| `table` | one of `goals`, `checkIns`, `plan`, `requests`, `people` | no | Which data table, when not using a view. |
| `columns` | list of string | no | The columns, in order. Leave out for the usual columns. |
| `query` | string | no | Search, filters and sort, as for save_table_view. |
| `format` | one of `csv`, `json` | no | CSV text, or rows as JSON. |

<details><summary>The input schema, as JSON</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "view": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The name of a saved layout: one of yours, or one pinned for everyone."
    },
    "table": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Which data table, when not using a view.",
      "enum": [
        "goals",
        "checkIns",
        "plan",
        "requests",
        "people"
      ]
    },
    "columns": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "The columns, in order. Leave out for the usual columns."
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Search, filters and sort, as for save_table_view."
    },
    "format": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "CSV text, or rows as JSON.",
      "enum": [
        "csv",
        "json"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

**Gives back:** the text, and `data`, one of:

```ts
{
    table: DataTable;
    columns: Cell[];
    rows: {
        [k: string]: string | number | null;
    }[];
}
```

```ts
{
    table: DataTable;
    columns: Cell[];
    count: number;
}
```

**Refuses with:**

- “There’s no saved layout called “…” that you can see. Use list_views.”
- “Say which table: ….”
- “… Its columns: ….”

**Does the same as:** no action: it reads, or does something only an assistant needs.
